- If sentiment is consistently bullish (positive) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently bearish (negative), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 3–5% in the following 3–5 days.  
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to historical mean after volatility), check if sentiment is neutral or mixed — if so, avoid over-correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates upward momentum in bullish sentiment cycles — increase forecast by 1–3% if sentiment > 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model often lags — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the next 2–3 days.  
- If model consistently forecasts lower than true outcome in 30-day horizon, check if sentiment is positive — if yes, increase forecast by 1–2% for next 30d.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to over-forecast — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 30d.
